reason: Conversation 1 hit the sensible first steps the ground truth expects: it addressed the rocking/levelling (including the wooden-floor factor and shimming without lifting), worked to localise the noise front vs rear with practical standing-up methods, had the customer turn the drum by hand, and then escalated appropriately to a repairer once the back injury and basic tools were disclosed, while keeping diagnosis hedged across jockey pulley, rollers, felts and belt. Conversation 2 was safe and honest and also escalated correctly, but it never explored levelling or where the noise originates - two of the stated important unknowns - and asked fewer useful questions before defaulting to an engineer. Both unplugged first and neither raised the condensate pump; Conversation 1's part-searching advice was slightly premature but was framed conditionally and superseded by the engineer recommendation, and its added recall check and warning signs were a bonus.
